overview.text: The Red-bellied Black Snake is a venomous snake of eastern Australia and one of the snakes people there meet most often. It is not aggressive and usually moves away from people.

identification.text: Glossy black on top with bright red or orange sides fading to a pink or dull red belly; light grey snout and a black tail.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Eastern Australia: Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia - including the areas around Brisbane, Sydney, Canberra, Melbourne and Adelaide.

habitat.text: Woodland, bushland, plains and urban forest, often near water.

behaviour.text: Hides in logs, old burrows and grass tussocks, and can escape into water - one stayed under for 23 minutes. In spring males wrestle each other, trying to push the other's head down.

diet.text: Mostly frogs, but also reptiles and other prey.

funfacts.text: It can float still on the water so that it looks just like a stick.

recognise.text: Shiny black back with red or orange sides.
